Many of the source types have similar day type distributions as the MOVES defaults when FleetDNA and CE-CERT are combined. For example, refuse trucks on urban freeways have 76% of miles driven on weekdays, just like MOVES defaults. However, on all other road types, refuse trucks drive significantly more on weekdays compared to MOVES, with 92% of urban other road driving occurring on weekdays and 100% of rural driving taking place on weekdays, albeit from only three vehicles’ data. Urban other road data for refuse trucks are relatively robust, and we recommend updating this proportion in MOVES. For combination-unit short-haul vehicles, we see slightly more time driven on weekdays on urban roads at 80% compared to 76% in MOVES, as well as rural freeway travel being 75% on weekdays to MOVES’ 72%; rural freeways are the exception for this source, spending less time driving on weekdays at only 64%. All combination-unit short-haul day VMT fractions can be incorporated into MOVES. Single- unit short-haul vehicles hover around the 76% of MOVES, spending slightly more time on weekdays on urban other roads and slightly less than MOVES on urban freeways; both urban road types can inform edits to MOVES. Possibly due to less data, single-unit short-haul day distributions are more extreme on rural roads, spending only 68% of driving time on weekdays for rural freeways and a high 89% on weekdays for rural other roads. We do not recommend incorporating single-unit short-haul rural data due to low data counts, unless it represents an improvement over MOVES non-source-specific distributions. Transit buses spend 73% of their time traveling on weekdays on urban other roads, but only 64% of urban freeway travel is completed on weekdays, and both can inform MOVES defaults. We observe even less weekday travel for transit buses on rural roads, although only two buses contributed to transit bus rural aggregates and should not be used in MOVES. School buses have all their activity on weekdays. Although our sample is limited, we believe this behavior best characterizes the activity of school buses and recommend MOVES defaults be updated to have all school bus activity occurring on weekdays. Other buses drive on urban freeways slightly more than MOVES defaults predict, and on urban other roads they drive much less on weekdays than MOVES at 53%. Due to small sample size, we do not recommend their incorporation into MOVES. In contrast to MOVES defaults and the other source types, combination-unit long-haul trucks show a significantly larger share of driving occurring on weekends compared to weekdays. Long-haul trucks typically drive trips over several days to deliver freight, and this often includes weekends.
